subject: Re: Burst forecast handshake — predictive autoscale + preemptive fallback proposal
content:
From: Maya Ramesh <maya.ramesh@atlasbio.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: AtlasBio Ops <ops@atlasbio.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Burst capacity ask ahead of Q1 peak

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we discussed, AtlasBio expects a concentrated run of inference jobs starting mid-Jan for the Q1 cohort: 72-hour windows, multiple simultaneous pipelines, and several large-batch retrains. Our SREs put a preliminary estimate in the attached spreadsheet (atlasbio-burst-req.xlsx) — nominally +140% peak over baseline for short windows, with many short-lived spikes.

Key asks:
- Can Redwood provide a predictive burst posture (pre-warmed shoulder + transient GPU slab) that minimizes cold-start latency?
- We want a documented fallback sequence if reserved pool pressure hits preemption: which model variants, how much headroom, and what our expected latency delta is.
- Is there a commercial crediting approach (short-duration top-ups) instead of re-negotiating the monthly commit?

We'd like a brief proposal by next Tue (2026-12-08) so we can align procurement with the run schedule.

Thanks,
Maya
Maya Ramesh
Head of Platform Eng, AtlasBio

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramesh <maya.ramesh@atlasbio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Burst capacity ask ahead of Q1 peak

Maya — thanks, this is helpful. Attaching an initial operational sketch; Ben and Lauren are looped for tech + commercial gaps.

High level proposal (summary):
- Predictive prewarm: for customer-configured windows we pre-warm an ephemeral slab (GPU instances) based on 12h rolling forecast from request patterns + scheduled jobs (customer-provided calendar).
- Shoulder reserve: a small reserved shoulder (~20% of the requested burst) that stays warm for the whole window to absorb micro-spikes with <150ms cold-start improvement vs purely on-demand.
- Transient slab: the remainder allocated as ephemeral nodes with 30-120s startup — we recommend concurrency throttling to smooth token-level latency.
- Fallback sequence: 1) route to quantized variant (same model arch, 8-bit) with priority for short-latency traffic; 2) spill to another region failover (if enabled); 3) best-effort queued execution with an SLA-exempt marker and customer alerting. We will document expected p50/p95 delta per step.

Commercial options to avoid commit changes:
- Short-term burst credits pool (pre-burned) that AtlasBio can draw on. Credits are priced at a premium but avoid renegotiation.
- Usage-based top-ups during the run window (metered, invoiced after).

Action items:
- Ben: can you sketch the kernel selection / prewarm ramp (startup times per GPU tier) and the KV cache warm-up expectations?
- Lauren: can you provide the crediting quotes and a short term amendment we can sign?
- Maya: confirm the schedule and any job calendars you can share.

I'll add a short runbook doc and an example fallback timeline by EOD Mon.

—Karthik

---

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Maya Ramesh <maya.ramesh@atlasbio.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 7 Dec 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Burst capacity ask ahead of Q1 peak

Maya / team,

Attached is a technical appendix (predictive-autoscale-config.yaml) and a short note on timings. Highlights:
- Cold-start by tier: A100-80GB (container + model load) ~ 45s median; H100-80GB ~ 28s; g5x2-ish prewarmed container path ~ 12-18s. We can reach sub-10s for tokenizer-only warm paths when KV cache is shared.
- KV cache strategy: checkpoint pre-warm for pinned variants; we recommend hybrid: keep KV cache for the shoulder-reserve and progressively spill ephemeral nodes.
- Ramp algorithm: we use a conservatively biased forecast (alpha=0.75) and a 15-min smoothing window; for AtlasBio's pattern I recommend a 2-stage ramp (fast + sustain) to avoid excessive churn.
- Eviction behavior: ephemeral slab will apply LRU preemption; we can tag high-priority routes to be last-evicted.

Impacts on latency (estimated):
- If we fall back to 8-bit quantized variant: expect +8-12% p50 token latency, p95 inflation dependent on batch sizes.
- Regional spill: added network RTT + model cold-start; recommend as last resort for ultra-low-latency customers.

I'll be available for a technical sync Wed if you want to walk through the YAML.

Ben
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: predictive-autoscale-config.yaml (see attached)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Maya Ramesh <maya.ramesh@atlasbio.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Burst capacity ask ahead of Q1 peak

Maya,

Thanks for the detail — pricing options below (high level):
- Option A (Credits Pool): one-time purchase of burst credits covering up to 200% of baseline for 7 days. Price = 1.9x standard on-demand rate. Credits draw down in real-time; leftover credits refundable within 30d at 50% of face value.
- Option B (Metered Top-up): metered usage during the event invoiced post-run; estimated premium multiplier 1.35x. Requires a signed short-term amendment for SLA carveouts.
- Option C (Temporary commit uplift): short-term uplift to committed monthly capacity (30-day ramp) priced as an addendum to your existing Dedicated contract.

We can draft the short amendment and a one-page runbook appendix for approval. If you want near-instant sign (DocuSign) we can get credit pool live within 48h of signature.

Next steps (commercial + ops):
- Maya: pick preferred pricing path by EOD Mon (2026-12-13).
- Karthik/Ben: finalize runbook and expected latency deltas.
- I'll issue a draft amendment and DocuSign link once you select an option.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
